title: A rail line's signal bundles and platforms

blocks.text: A regional rail line plans its works for 2027 to 2030. The model in `rail.py` has a binary `x[pid, t]` for each project and each year `t` in its `starts`, and it already says that no project starts twice. Two rules remain:

items: **Signal blocks.** Each list in `blocks` is a block of signal upgrades that one crew commissions together: either every upgrade of the block is done, all starting in the same year, or none is.

**Platforms.** `platforms` maps a platform extension to the track upgrades that can carry its longer trains. A platform extension may start in year `t` only if at least one of its track upgrades started in year `t - 1` or earlier.

blocks.text: Write `add_works_rules(model, x, projects, blocks, platforms)` so that the model allows exactly the plans that keep both rules.
The model so far, with $`P`$ the projects and $`T_i`$ the start years of project $`i`$:

Name the remaining sets (the blocks, the years every member of a block may start in, each platform's track upgrades) and write your rows, each with its quantifier and a label, before you code them. Ask what a block member's variable for a year that another member cannot use must be.

A sum over a set that can be empty, such as a project's start years up to `t`, is the number 0 in Python, and MathOpt refuses a row with no variable on either side. Skip such a row, or start the sum from `mathopt.LinearExpression()` (lesson 6.4.1).
The tests fix every `x[pid, t]` through its bounds and ask the solver whether the model accepts the plan, so any correct formulation passes. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from datetime import timedelta

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from rail import Project, build

works = [
    Project("SIG-X1", (2031, 2032)),
    Project("SIG-X2", (2032, 2033)),
    Project("STN-E", (2032, 2033)),
    Project("TRK-9", (2031, 2032, 2033)),
]
blocks = [["SIG-X1", "SIG-X2"]]
platforms = {"STN-E": ["TRK-9"]}

def solve_ok(model):
    params = mathopt.SolveParameters(time_limit=timedelta(seconds=5))
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=params)
    return result.termination.reason == mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL


def allowed(plan):
    model, x = build(works, blocks, platforms)
    for key, var in x.items():
        value = 1.0 if key in plan else 0.0
        if value > var.upper_bound:
            return False
        var.lower_bound = var.upper_bound = value
    return solve_ok(model)


print("SIG-X1 and SIG-X2 in 2032:", allowed({("SIG-X1", 2032), ("SIG-X2", 2032)}))
print("SIG-X1 in 2031 alone:", allowed({("SIG-X1", 2031)}))
print("SIG-X1 2031, SIG-X2 2032:", allowed({("SIG-X1", 2031), ("SIG-X2", 2032)}))
print("TRK-9 2031, STN-E 2032:", allowed({("TRK-9", 2031), ("STN-E", 2032)}))
print("TRK-9 2032, STN-E 2032:", allowed({("TRK-9", 2032), ("STN-E", 2032)}))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    starts: tuple[int, ...]


def add_works_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, projects: list[Project], blocks: list[list[str]],
                    platforms: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None:
    """Signal blocks done whole and in one year; each platform after one of its track upgrades."""
    # TODO: the block rows and the platform rows.
    return None


def build(projects: list[Project], blocks: list[list[str]],
          platforms: dict[str, list[str]]) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="rail-works")
    x = {(p.pid, t): model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}_{t}") for p in projects for t in p.starts}
    for p in projects:
        model.add_linear_constraint(sum(x[p.pid, t] for t in p.starts) <= 1, name=f"once_{p.pid}")
    add_works_rules(model, x, projects, blocks, platforms)
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    projects = [Project("SIG1", (2027, 2028)), Project("SIG2", (2028,)), Project("PLAT", (2029,)),
                Project("TRK", (2027, 2028))]
    model, x = build(projects, [["SIG1", "SIG2"]], {"PLAT": ["TRK"]})
    print(model.get_num_linear_constraints(), "rows")

cases.says: a block upgraded whole is allowed, and one upgraded in part is refused
a platform extension after one of its track upgrades is allowed, and one with no track upgrade is refused
a block whose members start in different years is refused
one track upgrade is enough for a platform; both are not required
a track upgrade started in the platform's own year does not count

origin.section: A Bundle That Starts Together Is an Equality per Year

concepts: a bundle ties each member's started sum to one member's
a child may have started by a year only if its parent, or one of its parents, had started by then
a same-year bundle ties start variables year by year and fixes the years not every member can use
